Moth and Gravel. Field Note 17.
The Grid is Shared. An AI

narrated edition of the
published note. A cattle, a hot

water tank, a room of servers.
Very different work carried

through the same electricity
system. Finland's appeal to a

data center developer is easy to
put on a slide. A cool climate,

clean electricity, room to
build. At home, the question

arrives in smaller print. The
price on a contract renewal. The

network charge. The housing
company's heating budget. We

wanted to follow the connection
that far. The resulting Finnish

account opens three records.
Household electricity prices,

national power flows, and heat
delivered in Mansala. Each keeps

its own date and boundary. Put
them beside one another and the

public question becomes more
precise. Who pays for the

connection? Who can change their
demand? And who receives the

useful heat? The bill has three
parts. The price discussed in an

electricity market headline is
only part of what a household

pays. There is the electricity
sold, the network service, and

tax. A resident can choose an
electricity seller. The local

distribution network comes with
the address. KKV's consumer

guidance makes that distinction
explicit. Our first account uses

Statistics Finland's table 13
RB. Take January 2024, consumer

band C for annual use between
2500 and 4999 kilowatt hours.

Choose an illustrative 3000
kilowatt hours a year and hold

that month's published rates
constant. January 2024 rates.

Band C. An assumed 3000 kilowatt
hour year. Energy excluding tax.

10.880 cents per kilowatt hour.
Annualized, 326 Euros and 40

cents. Network excluding tax.
7.532 cents per kilowatt hour.

Annualized, 225 Euros and 96
cents. Tax including excise and

VAT. 7.213 cents per kilowatt
hour. Annualized, 216 Euros and

39 cents. Published total
including
tax.

cents. The arithmetic is annual
KWH multiplied by cents per

kilowatt hour divided by 100.
The already included tax, we add

neither another layer of VAT nor
separate fixed charges to this

published unit price statistic.
768 Euros and 75 cents is an

illustration at one month's
national consumer band rates. It

is neither a measured household
bill nor the cost of consuming

electricity throughout 2024 at
the prices that actually

occurred. The distinction
matters before we ask a future

price to explain anything. A
simple sensitivity is useful

here. If a VAT inclusive retail
energy rate were 1 cent per

kilowatt hour higher, a home
using 20,000 kilowatt hours

would pay 200 Euros more over a
year with use and every other

charge held constant. At 3000
kilowatt hours, the difference

would be 30 Euros. These are
conditional multiplications. We

have supplied no evidence that
data centers cause that 1 cent

change. Additional demand has to
meet electricity available at

the same time and through a
network able to carry it. Its

effect on prices depends on the
supply response, whether

imports, outages, location, and
the load's ability to move. New

demand can support new
generation investment. A promise

of future generation still needs
a commissioning date. Fingrid

reported in August 2026 that
data center projects with signed

connection agreements had a
planned final combined capacity

of nearly 5 gigawatts including
distribution network

connections. That is a project
capacity figure. It does not

mean 5 gigawatts was already
drawing power continuously. To

see why the distinction matters,
assume a whole facility load of

100 megawatts operating
constantly for an ordinary 8760

hour year. It consumes 876,000
megawatt hours or 0.876 terawatt

hours. This is arithmetic, not a
surveyed Finnish facility. A

nameplate, an annual energy
total, and the demand on a cold

evening are three different
descriptions. The Ministry of

Economic Affairs and
Employment's October 2026

account acknowledges both the
opportunity for new production

and regional network scarcity.
National abundance does not

establish room at a particular
substation. Our grid view

replays two recorded weeks, one
in January and one in July 2024

from Energiateollisuus hourly
data. Consumption reconciles

with domestic production plus
imports and signed exports. Wind

is already inside production.
The source clock stays at UTC +2

including July. Adding a chosen
facility draw makes an extra

requirement visible beside the
historical hour. We hold

historical supply fixed. The
dashed line cannot tell us which

plant would respond, what the
market would charge, or whether

a connection would be permitted.
Exporting electricity in a

recorded hour is also no proof
of spare network capacity at a

proposed site. This is where an
annual renewable energy claim

needs another question. What
happens in the hours the

contracted generation is absent?
A useful answer specifies

timing, balancing, transmission,
and the demand that can actually

be deferred. Flexibility belongs
to someone. Households will

adjust can sound painless at the
scale of a national chart. At

home, it means deciding when the
water heats, whether the car can

wait, whether a room can be
cooler. A home with a

controllable heat pump, an
insulated envelope, and money

for improvements has options
that a tenant may be unable to

buy or install. A low bill
achieved by giving something up

deserves a different label from
the same bill achieved by better

equipment. There is Finnish
research on this uneven room to

move. Lassi Alvik, Tomas
KariAho, Matti Lisk

and Ivo Vevilainens 2025 working
paper on the European energy

crisis uses the timing of
expiring two year fixed price

contracts to study Finnish
households during 2022.

The authors find that lower
income households have fewer

ways to adjust with greater
financial distress and cuts in

other spending. This is a
working paper about a particular

price shock. It does not
estimate the future household

effect of Finnish data centers.
It does give us a reason to

distrust the idea of one
representative household with an

unlimited ability to shift
demand. A fixed price contract

can delay exposure to energy
price changes until renewal. A

spot priced contract exposes the
resident sooner to the timing of

use. Neither makes the network
charge disappear. The same

wholesale price development can
therefore reach two neighbors in

different months with different
consequences. For a large new

consumer, we would want
flexibility described just as

concretely. How many megawatts
can stop? For how long? With how

much notice? What happens when
the work resumes? Who verifies

delivery? An interruptible
commitment has public value only

to the extent that it can be
used when the system needs it. A

demonstration on an easy day
leaves that question open.

The cable has an account too. A
new connection can bring

investment, work, and demand for
electricity that helps finance

production. It can also require
reinforcement. The household

question is how the costs and
benefits are divided across the

connection charge, network
tariffs, the developer, and any

public support. We cannot infer
that division from the size of a

building or from a national
consumption trace. It needs the

applicable connection terms, the
reinforcement plan, and the

regulated network account. A
claim that households will pay

for everything is as incomplete
as a claim that they will pay

for nothing. According to KKV,
the energy authority supervises

network pricing as a whole over
four year periods using a

reasonable return framework.
This is not a cap on each

individual tariff. The existence
of supervision does not remove

the need to inspect how a
particular expansion is funded.

For a municipality considering a
project, we would put the dates

beside the money. When does the
facility start using power? When

is the reinforcement available?
Who bears a delay? Which

25.625 cents per kilowatt hour.
Annualized, 768 Euros and 75

spending is committed if the
campus is built in phases or

remains smaller than announced?
Those are terms a resident

should be able to understand
without becoming an electricity

market analyst. They are also
terms a project can publish

before asking its neighbors to
trust a distant benefit.

Follow the heat to a building.
Heat recovery is the most

tangible part of the promise.
Somewhere, a radiator becomes

warm. To follow that promise, we
need a pipe, an operating

system, and a measured delivery.
The 2024 district heating

statistics give us a reported
Nivosa Vesi Yalampo account for
Mansala covering several

networks. On the supply side,
31.5 gigawatt hours of other net

heat production and 22.7
gigawatt hours in a combined

recovery heat pump category make
54.2 gigawatt hours. On the

other side, Nivosa Mansala 2024.
Thermal energy in gigawatt

hours. Residential buildings,
16.0 gigawatt hours. Industry,

0.4 gigawatt hours. Other
customers, 32.1 gigawatt hours.

All customer use, 48.5 gigawatt
hours. Network losses and meter

differences, 5.7. Total supplied
heat, 54.2 gigawatt hours.

16.0 + 0.4 + 32.1 = 48.5. Add
5.7 and the account returns to

54.2. The 115 residential
customers reported alongside

these figures are building
accounts, not 115 households.

The recovery category does not
isolate pure server waste heat.

Nor does the table allocate
particular heat sources to

particular homes. We can say
that residential buildings used

16.0 gigawatt hours. We cannot
say that data center heat

supplied that entire amount. A
heat pump adds its own

electricity to the recovered
heat. Distribution then has its

own losses. Thermal kilowatt
hours delivered and electrical

kilowatt hours consumed must
keep their separate meters.

Subtracting one from the other
would conceal the system we are

trying to understand. There is a
seasonal question too. Useful

heat depends on temperature,
demand, and the alternative

source it displaces. A
year-round server load does not

come with year-round winter
heating demand. Storage, hot

water, and other users may help,
but their capacity and operation

need evidence of their own. A
percentage needs an address. The

Nivosa report for 2025 records
company-wide heat sales of 43.1

gigawatt hours. A separate
origin disclosure gives

recovered surplus heat a 41%
share in the central Mansala

network that year. The
boundaries differ. Multiplying

43.1 by 41% would produce a neat
number with no matching

published account bill behind
it. We leave that multiplication

undone. Commissioning language
needs the same care. Fortum's

May 2026 announcement says its
plants at the Espoo and

Kirkkonummi data center sites
had begun producing heat from

ambient air and electric
boilers. The release schedules

data center waste heat
integration to begin in stages

in 2027. A plant operating at a
data center site does not by

itself means server heat has
already reached a home.

Even a measured heat benefit has
a distribution question. It

reaches properties connected to
the relevant network. Living

nearby does not make a detached
home part of that system. For a

housing company or tenant, a
lower production cost still

needs a route through the heat
tariff, building costs, and

household charges. There is
something concrete to inspect in

Mansala. Nivosa reports a 15%
cut in the summer energy charge

from the 1st of May 2025 and a
5% cut in the winter energy

charge from the 1st of January
2026.

These are particular tariff
components and dates. They are

neither equivalent cuts to every
customer's total annual bill nor

proof that recovered heat alone
caused the reductions. The

useful promise would name the
network, the delivered quantity,

the season, the alternative heat
source, and the tariff

consequence. Then a resident can
follow it beyond a rendering of

a pipe. Rules, with something to
inspect, Finland is not starting

from an absence of rules. As
checked on the 23rd of October

2026, the tax administration
says data center electricity

moved from tax class two to
class one on the 1st of July

2026. That change is separate
from both the household's

historical price record and a
forecast of future market

prices. The energy efficiency
amendment effective from January

2026 also contains heat reuse
duties. Section 29E applies

above 1 megawatt of total power.
For existing centers with no

reuse, technical or economic
infeasibility must be

demonstrated through a
cost-benefit analysis. The first

notification under that
provision is due by the 31st of

December 2027. Related
provisions address analysis for

new or substantially refurbished
centers. This is more specific

than a universal percentage of
heat that every site must sell.

EU regulation 2024/1364
establishes reporting for data

centers with at least 500
kilowatts of installed IT power.

Its public database information
is aggregated. Individual

facility submissions are kept
confidential. A reporting

requirement does not
automatically give a neighbor

the local account we have been
following. Our interest is in

what can be checked afterwards.
A connection agreement should

remain distinguishable from a
working load. An offered

interruption should leave a
delivery record. A heat

agreement should lead to a
delivered energy account. A

claimed household saving should
identify the charge that changed

and the homes that can receive
it. These are design

requirements as much as research
questions. Dates beside

percentages, units beside
numbers, assumptions that remain

attached when an account is
exported. A missing residential

breakdown shown as missing
without a reassuring estimate

quietly taking its place. The
room of servers can be useful.

The recovered heat can be
useful. The people outside

should be able to inspect the
terms on which those things

become useful to them. The grid
is shared. The account should be

readable from home. Method,
sources, limits. Three records,

separate boundaries, written and
checked the 23rd of October
2026.

The working specimen opens the
source records and exports the

selection with its assumptions,
source locations, and hashes.

The provenance manifest and
reproduction instructions

preserve the numerical method.
This note estimates no causal

effect of data centers on
finished prices, network

tariffs, or household welfare.

Energy sums hourly mean MW
multiplied by 1 hour. This

differs from the point sample

establish neither local headroom

nor a future dispatch response.

Evidence about the 2022 crisis,

Proposals, targets, and

treated as observed deliveries.

follows recorded power inside a

household price or local heat
figure is inferred from that

room. You have been listening to
